title: California ZIP codes with greater FAIR Plan share also show higher voluntary-market nonrenewal among renewal decisions
source_unit: California Department of Insurance ZIP-level voluntary-market policy counts crosswalked to FAIR Plan residential-structure share

denominator.unit: valid ZIP-year rows in California Department of Insurance voluntary-market file

observations.method: Summed California Department of Insurance ZIP-level counts for new, renewed, and non-renewed residential policies; calculated nonrenewal share among renewed plus non-renewed decisions.
observations.uncertainty: The file reports counts, not unique households, reasons, coverage limits, premiums, claims, or later outcomes. CDI notes a change in some nonrenewal/cancellation categories beginning in 2020.
observations.subgroup: California voluntary residential market across ZIP codes and the published policy forms; HO-4 and HO-6 are excluded.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower statewide nonrenewal share in 2023 than 2020 does not rule out severe local or risk-specific pressure; changes in composition and reporting definitions can affect the aggregate.

denominator.unit: ZIP rows in California DOI FAIR-versus-voluntary residential-structure PDF

joined_zip_rows.unit: rows also present in voluntary-market ZIP file

observations.method: ZIP-code text match between the California DOI FAIR-versus-voluntary 2022 residential-structure table and the 2022 rows in the DOI voluntary-market workbook.
observations.uncertainty: The FAIR table counts residential dwelling structures and excludes some property types; the voluntary workbook covers a broader policy-form universe. The join does not make the denominators identical.
observations.subgroup: California ZIP codes with at least the source's reported residential-structure coverage; ZIP codes with fewer than five FAIR-insured structures were excluded by CDI.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high matching rate reflects geographic coverage, not equivalence of policy universes or evidence that the same structures appear in both measures.

observations.period: 2022; lowest versus highest quartile of FAIR residential-structure share

denominator.unit: joined ZIP rows split into equal-count lowest/highest FAIR-share quartiles; voluntary renewal decisions

lowest_quartile_mean_fair_share.unit: percent of residential structures insured by FAIR, mean of ZIP percentages

highest_quartile_mean_fair_share.unit: percent of residential structures insured by FAIR, mean of ZIP percentages

lowest_quartile_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus non-renewed decisions

highest_quartile_nonrenewal_rate.unit: percent among voluntary renewed plus non-renewed decisions

observations.method: Joined ZIP rows sorted by published FAIR-share percentage; the lowest and highest equal-count quartiles were compared using voluntary nonrenewed/(renewed+nonrenewed) counts.
observations.uncertainty: Quartile means are unweighted by structures and policy count, and ZIP composition, hazard, property, and insurer mix are uncontrolled.
observations.subgroup: ZIP rows in the bottom and top quarter of published FAIR residential-structure share.
observations.counterinterpretation: The association may reflect wildfire risk, property mix, market composition, or reporting thresholds; it does not establish that FAIR enrollment causes nonrenewal or that individual policyholders moved between markets.

related_sources.claim: California DOI describes its annual ZIP counts and FAIR Plan share data, including coverage and exclusions.
related_sources.access_boundary: The page does not create a same-household longitudinal market transition.

related_sources.claim: Local analysis output records the ZIP match and quartile calculations.
related_sources.access_boundary: The crosswalk is descriptive and denominator-mismatched.

boundary: This record establishes a descriptive ZIP-level association between FAIR Plan share and voluntary-market nonrenewal decisions in 2022, alongside statewide voluntary-market counts for 2020-2023. It does not establish causal private-market withdrawal, household affordability, coverage adequacy, claims, repairs, mobility, or political response.
